limitations_and_boundaries: The theoretical equivalence between GNNs and 1-WL holds for a broad class of architectures but assumes suitable parameter initialization.
k-GNN models have more parameters than 1-GNN; extending 1-GNN with additional layers to match parameters did not improve results.
The benefit of higher-order structure varies significantly across regression targets.
Experiments on graph classification used small benchmark datasets; recent advanced pooling techniques were not combined with k-GNN layers.
The QM9 experiments used only pairwise Euclidean distances for connected nodes, not a complete graph with distance annotations.
